stories.headline: Rays beat Guardians 7-3, win ALCS and head to the World Series
stories.summary: Junior Caminero and Yandy Díaz homered and Freddy Peralta pitched 5 1/3 innings as Tampa Bay took the series 4-2. The Rays face the Milwaukee Brewers in their first full-season World Series since 2008.

stories.headline: AI stocks lead a rebound as the Nasdaq gains 1.1%
stories.summary: The Nasdaq rose 1.11% to 26,430.89 and the S&P 500 0.41% to 7,690.73 after last week's worst week since June, while the Dow slipped 0.07%; most stocks outside AI and tech fell, and seven of 11 S&P sectors closed lower.

stories.headline: Houthi missiles kill at least 53 at Yemeni government camp
stories.summary: Houthi rebels fired ballistic missiles at the al-Alam military camp in Shabwa province Monday, killing at least 53 soldiers, one of the deadliest attacks since a 2022 ceasefire collapsed. Oil rose on the news.

stories.headline: France orders local curfews after a weekend of rioting and looting
stories.summary: PM Sébastien Lecornu told prefects to impose limited curfews after violence targeting city halls and businesses led to 2,400 arrests on Sunday; European stocks fell more than 1%.

stories.headline: Court weighs lawsuit against Amendment 87 two weeks before Election Day
stories.summary: A Denver court is hearing a lawsuit that could affect the graduated income tax measure's place on the November ballot, a statewide question for Highlands Ranch voters too.

breadth.label: Percent of S&P 500 stocks above 50-day MA
breadth.note: Below 30 bullish, above 70 bearish. Computed by Thaddeus from Yahoo Finance daily closes for 502 of 503 current S&P 500 constituents at the Oct. 19 close (mimics MMFI).

fear_greed.commentary: Sentiment stayed stuck at 23, in extreme fear, despite Monday's tech bounce, down from 44 a week ago. A narrow, AI-led rally with breadth slipping to 43.8% didn't convince the broader market.

markets.summary: A narrow bounce: the Nasdaq gained 1.1% and NVDA 1.4% as AI and chip stocks recovered some of last week's losses, but the Dow slipped 0.07% and most stocks outside tech fell, with utilities (-2%) and real estate (-1.2%) the laggards. Breadth eased to 43.8% of S&P 500 stocks above their 50-day average. Small caps barely moved, with the Russell 2000 up about 0.3% to 2,728. Rates remain the headwind: the 10-year Treasury yield rose about 7 basis points to 5.14% as bond traders brace for a possible Fed hike on energy-driven inflation, with WTI crude settling up 2.2% at $103.66. Gold futures slipped 0.5% to $4,160 and silver held near $56.97; both remain below their 40-week averages.

stories.headline: SpaceX reports Q3 results after Tuesday's close
stories.summary: Analysts expect revenue of roughly $12.7-12.9 billion, up from $7.81 billion in Q2, and a return to profit; AI spending, capex and Starlink growth are the focus.

stories.headline: Nvidia rebounds ahead of a major earnings week
stories.summary: Shares reached $216.51 Monday as investors returned to AI stocks; Nvidia closed at $217.09, up 1.4%.

stories.headline: Barclays trims Cameco target to $95
stories.summary: Barclays kept an Equal-Weight rating on Cameco and lowered its price target to $95 from $97.

weather.summary: The nor'easter off the Carolinas keeps moderate coastal flooding, beach erosion and dangerous seas going from southern New Jersey to the North Carolina coast into midweek, with gusts over 45 mph possible on the Outer Banks and Virginia Tidewater. Out West, a low sliding down the coast sends a plume of moisture into California and the Southwest Tuesday, with showers and thunderstorms; WPC has a Slight Risk (level 2 of 4) of excessive rainfall for parts of the Southwest, Great Basin and Central/Southern Rockies Wednesday into Thursday morning, with flash flooding most likely on burn scars, in canyons and in urban areas. Scattered rain and storms continue over Florida's east coast and the Keys and over far South Texas through Wednesday.
